author: Arjun Brij
title: Federation of Indian Pilots Seeks Formal Nomination to AI-171 Draft Report Review Committee
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Sep 27, 2026 | Updated 02:07 PM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
The Federation of Indian Pilots has written to Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu requesting formal representation in any independent review of the draft final investigation report into the Air India AI-171 crash.
The pilots' body asked to be nominated as an independent technical participant in the review mechanism, citing concerns over the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's expertise in examining the June 2025 disaster that killed 260 people.
In its letter dated 25 September, FIP stated it had learnt the government was considering requiring the draft report to undergo examination by an independent committee before finalisation.
The organisation requested formal nomination if such a review mechanism is constituted, arguing that professional pilots should critically evaluate technical aspects of the inquiry.
The request follows an earlier FIP submission to the AAIB last week seeking comprehensive evaluation of electrical-system evidence related to Boeing 787 aircraft.
The Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad on 12 June 2025 during a flight to London Gatwick. Of the 242 people aboard, 241 were killed, with all 12 crew members amongst the dead.
Another 19 people on the ground also died. FIP raised concerns that key technical discrepancies identified during the probe should be independently examined before findings are finalised.
The AAIB informed the Supreme Court in July that the final investigation report was expected by October 2026. Neither the civil aviation ministry nor the AAIB have issued immediate comments on FIP's request.
The pilots' organisation emphasised its request focuses on adding professional pilot representation to the review process rather than replacing the statutory investigation being conducted by the AAIB.
Arjun Brij is a Newsroom Associate at Swarajya. He tracks infrastructure and trade developments and posts on X at @arjun_brij.
